items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Ross Russell was friendly with my parents... he’s staying — you know there’s my bed and there’s a rollaway cot and it’s Ross Russell in our apartment

ctx.x: Right. How did you find them overall as people?

Well everybody’s different. And I can separate their identities. I believe there is a reason why Basie got these groups together. I believe they are individuals who created a connectable core to each other. I find the camaraderie of the Basie guys, it’s a moot point now except maybe in some larger sense, but there was a buddy system there that’s different from — but they’re all different. Eddie Durham for instance, probably was musically the most smart, best trained, clearly a genius. I would go so far to say…

first electric guitarist. He arranged “In the Mood” for Glenn Miller. He wrote the original Basie band book. He taught all these people. He wrote “Topsy,” he co-wrote the “One O’clock Jump” he really created the formula and he was very, very — not so much introverted as incredibly quiet and had no arguing desires in his make-up. I used to have these things I would mention to Eddie and he would tweak them for me. In a sense he would correct me, and then I would stick with my answer. And he would say, “Okay, Phil.”…
